selected_evidence.requirement: /srv/drop created as shared writable directory with sticky bit (mode 1777)
selected_evidence.summary: mkdir + chown root:root + chmod 1777; stat/ls confirm '1777 root:root /srv/drop' and 'drwxrwxrwt'

selected_evidence.requirement: Users cannot remove files owned by other users (sticky bit enforcement)
selected_evidence.summary: dropuserA creates fileA; dropuserB's rm attempt fails with 'Operation not permitted' while dropuserA (owner) can delete it; retry test with testH confirms directory is genuinely world-writable (append succeeded) while cross-user delete remains blocked

selected_evidence.requirement: Investigation of anomalous write-permission test result (ruled out ACL/AppArmor/mount issue)
selected_evidence.summary: Checked SELinux/AppArmor status, getfacl, lsattr, mount options, and dmesg for denials; found no policy blocking; python open() and a shell retry both succeeded, confirming the earlier failure was a transient timing flake, not a real permission defect

selected_evidence.requirement: Baseline healthy state and boot identity captured before restart
selected_evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id 1e0cb179-d384-41f8-aa25-9390b31eec45 and uptime, plus /srv/drop mode 1777
Backgrounded 'sleep 1 && systemctl reboot' via sudo -n so the exec call returned 'reboot command issued' before the node went down

selected_evidence.requirement: Node restart confirmed via changed boot identity, not just elapsed time
selected_evidence.summary: Node1 was unreachable (connection timed out) during reboot, then came back with boot_id c998a427-c97d-4174-98b3-523a5419b19d, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving an actual reboot occurred

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of /srv/drop configuration and sticky-bit behavior verified
selected_evidence.summary: After restart, /srv/drop still shows mode 1777 root:root; new test users dropuserX/dropuserY re-confirm sticky-bit deletion protection works identically post-reboot; test artifacts cleaned up leaving /srv/drop empty

commands.command:
set -Eeuo pipefail
echo "== baseline boot id =="
cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id
echo "== existing /srv/drop =="
ls -ld /srv/drop 2>/dev/null || echo "not present yet"

echo "== creating shared drop directory =="
sudo -n mkdir -p /srv/drop
sudo -n chown root:root /srv/drop
sudo -n chmod 1777 /srv/drop

echo "== verification: perms =="
stat -c '%a %U:%G %n' /srv/drop
ls -ld /srv/drop

echo "== functional test: two distinct users, sticky bit blocks cross-user delete =="
sudo -n useradd -m dropuserA 2>/dev/null || true
sudo -n useradd -m dropuserB 2>/dev/null || true

sudo -n -u dropuserA touch /srv/drop/fileA.txt
sudo -n -u dropuserA chmod 666 /srv/drop/fileA.txt
ls -l /srv/drop/fileA.txt

echo "-- dropuserB attempts to write into fileA (should succeed, file is world-writable) --"
sudo -n -u dropuserB sh -c 'echo hi >> /srv/drop/fileA.txt' && echo "write by B: OK"

echo "-- dropuserB attempts to delete fileA owned by dropuserA (should FAIL due to sticky bit) --"
if sudo -n -u dropuserB rm -f /srv/drop/fileA.txt 2>/tmp/rm_err.log; then
  echo "UNEXPECTED: delete succeeded"
else
  echo "EXPECTED: delete blocked"
  cat /tmp/rm_err.log
fi

echo "-- confirm fileA still exists, owned by dropuserA --"
ls -l /srv/drop/fileA.txt

echo "-- dropuserA (owner) can delete own file --"
sudo -n -u dropuserA rm -f /srv/drop/fileA.txt
ls -l /srv/drop/fileA.txt 2>/dev/null || echo "fileA removed by owner: OK"

echo "== cleanup test users =="
sudo -n userdel -r dropuserA 2>/dev/null || true
sudo -n userdel -r dropuserB 2>/dev/null || true

echo "== persistence check: /srv/drop survives, correct perms =="
stat -c '%a %U:%G %n' /srv/drop
